purpose: Fixed mutation set for the number corpus. Hand-written entries are one exact source edit to a number helper; generated entries are enumerated from the helper's AST by the runner (refusal sites, refusal-guard predicates, relational boundaries) and committed here by key. Each mutant is built in memory as a fresh module; the number corpus must fail under it with its witness case among the failures. Declared survivors carry a reason for review. Run: python3 scripts/pm_event_numbers.py --self-test --scope numbers --mutations

rules_source: One row per documented non-refusal rule or single predicate of CV-1100, SP-1100 and SP-1101 (Plans/Contracts_V0.md, Plans/storage-plan.md) and the adoption guide's shared calls, with the existing profile owner where the rule is that owner's (CV-317, CV-339, CV-366, SP-337). Each rule names hand-written mutation ids or generated point keys.

rules.rule: Current JSON integer inputs are exactly 0 or -?[1-9][0-9]*: no leading zero.
No negative zero in a current integer token.
No plus sign in a current integer token.
No fraction or exponent in a current integer token.
The token grammar's [0-9] is ASCII digits only.
The whole token matches the grammar; no surrounding whitespace.
Current typed integer inputs require an exact integer primitive, excluding booleans.
... and excluding runtime floats; no silent float coercion.
No silent string coercion into an integer.
Field-specific minima still apply, inclusively.
Field-specific maxima still apply, inclusively.
Slot bounds apply on the token and JsonNumber routes too.
No decoder may narrow an integer through binary64.
No global maximum-safe ceiling (4400-digit integers stay exact).
loads_current_json never converts fractional or exponent tokens, even integral ones, to ints or floats.
An undeclared fractional token keeps its lexical float kind.
Optional schema numeric_kinds select the kind by exact path, including array indices.
numeric_kinds applies independently of the parser carrier: a declared kind overrides the carrier's own.
A bare Decimal has no implicit owner kind.
Raw JsonNumber preserves its integer/float token kind.
Kind preservation is judged on the emitted JCS token.
The emitted decimal must equal the original exact value (2^60).
The original integer must survive binary64 exactly (2^53+1).
Typed signed zero is not erased: a raw -0 token.
Typed signed zero is not erased: a Decimal carrier.
Typed signed zero is not erased: a runtime float.
sign_sensitive_paths checks zero sign without requiring a primitive kind.
Qualification paths are tuples of map keys and array indices from the original schema.
Actual RFC8785: keys in UTF-16 code-unit order.
Array order remains exactly owner-defined.
JCS strings and keys are Unicode scalar values.
No silent bool coercion: booleans stay JSON booleans.
Producer semantics use the unchanged full producer projection.
Producer routes qualify with the caller's type, sign and kind declarations.
The producer digest is lowercase hex SHA-256 of the JCS bytes.
EventRecord MessagePack integers span -2^63 through 2^64-1 inclusive.
Minimal type-preserving integer widths at every boundary.
General EventRecord floats retain float type even when integral.
Floats retain signed zero in float32 and float64.
float32 only with exact value preservation, and only for EventRecord; app physical is float64.
Minimal string headers (fixstr, str8, str16).
Minimal array and map headers (fixarray, fixmap).
Map keys in UTF-8 byte order (not the JCS UTF-16 order), on every profile.
Array order is preserved in physical bytes.
Physical strings are valid Unicode scalar values.
App binary takes the minimal bin8/bin16/bin32 header (255 vs 256, 65535 vs 65536, 2^32-1).
App binary is legal only in the app physical profile; EventRecord disallows binary.
Canonical decoding admits only string map keys.
Decoding rejects alternates according to the selected profile.
Decoded bytes must re-encode to the identical canonical bytes.
Payload byte sizes cover the exact original bytes.
Payload IDs are lowercase 64-hex BLAKE3 digests.
The inline limit admits exactly 16384 bytes.
The full-value commitment covers only pm.event.v0 2.0.0 events.
The unchanged CV-339 tuple order.
Every recipe tuple field is a non-empty string.
The resource manifest hash is lowercase 64-hex.
Every binding identity field is a non-empty string.
Application scope requires project_id null, not empty.
Project scope requires a non-empty project_id string.
One original selection: a non-empty string reference and an exact OriginalBinding.
The owner's binding is an exact OriginalBinding equal to the query.
Original record, result and receipt stay exact bytes.
The frozen verifier is selected by the original's own recipe tuple.
Only verifier result True authenticates; no truthy value.
Exactly one frozen verifier runs; no probing.
Current disclosure is checked independently and must be exactly True.
loads_exact refuses raw control characters in JSON strings.
Every parsed string and key is a Unicode scalar value.
Byte input is strict UTF-8.
current_append_policy admits exactly one of the three policy strings as an exact str.

families.refusal_site: Every raise statement and every _refuse(...) call, the only ways the helper emits an error code (returns, lambdas and except handlers included). The mutant disables that one site: a call becomes None, a raise becomes pass.
families.refusal_predicate: Every predicate of the if-guards of a _refuse site (each enclosing if whose body holds it) where dropping that predicate alone weakens the guard: an or-operand at positive polarity becomes False, an and-operand under not becomes True, and an element of a literal tuple scanned by any() is dropped.
families.comparison_boundary: Every <, <=, > and >= in the helper. The mutant flips strictness (< and <=, > and >=), the off-by-one at that width, range or limit boundary.

site:<module>:raise#1.survives: CLI entry point, not an API refusal: `raise SystemExit(main())` runs only under __main__, and the mutant module is loaded in memory, never as __main__. Without it the CLI would exit 0 on a failing corpus; the fresh-process CLI controls (a deliberately wrong expected output gives exit 1) cover the exit status instead.

boundary:qualified_jcs.number:math.copys.survives: Equivalent: math.copysign(1.0, f) returns exactly 1.0 or -1.0 (NaN included), never 0, so < 0 and <= 0 agree for every input.

boundary:storage_value_bytes:v >= 0:0#1.survives: Equivalent: with v > 0, the integer 0 takes the negative branch, whose fixint test (0 >= -32) emits bytes([0 & 255]) = 0x00, the same byte binding_bytes(0) emits.
